title: A Place at the King's Table
overview: King David keeps an old promise to his friend Jonathan by seeking out Jonathan's disabled son and giving him land and a lasting place in the royal household.

parts.label: David looks for Saul's family (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Years earlier David swore loyalty to his friend Jonathan, son of the former king Saul, and promised to care for Jonathan's family, so here he acts on that promise. In an age when new kings often wiped out the old royal family, David instead asks whom he can help.

parts.label: Mephibosheth is found (vv. 4-5)
parts.note: Saul's former servant Ziba reports that Jonathan has a son who has been unable to walk since a fall in childhood, when his nurse fled with him after Saul and Jonathan died. He has been living quietly east of the Jordan River in the home of a man named Makir, likely out of the public eye.

parts.label: Fear turns to welcome (vv. 6-8)
parts.note: Mephibosheth bows low, and David's first words telling him not to fear suggest he expected punishment or death as the old king's grandson. Calling himself a "dead dog" was a way of saying he was worthless and had no claim on the king.

parts.label: Land and servants given (vv. 9-10)
parts.note: David returns Saul's family estates to Mephibosheth and orders Ziba, with his fifteen sons and twenty servants, to farm the land for him. This gives Mephibosheth both an income and the standing of a noble household.

parts.label: Eating at the king's table (vv. 11-13)
parts.note: Eating at the king's table meant living in Jerusalem and being treated like one of David's own sons. Some scholars note it also kept a possible rival close at hand, and Christians have often read the scene as a picture of God welcoming people who feel they have no claim on him.

disagreement: Readers differ on whether David acted purely out of loyal love for Jonathan or whether keeping Saul's heir close at court was also a shrewd political move, and how much that matters for the story's meaning.
think: What would it take for you to trust kindness from someone you had good reason to fear?
